(edit - the lobbies are indeed fully dead now) Strengths first! Visuals. Games visual design is liminal. the level of polish in the map and certain bits of the audio / atmosphere really sell the game. Certain set pieces of this game are much more memorable than you’d expect them to be. The work here is beautiful. The snowy out door area got added from the trailer, but it's tiny. Sounds in the map are generally really strong too, and these two together can carry horror games, but here the audio plays through 8 walls like it's in the same room. The issues. Enemies. The enemies are really clunky, the ai is exceedingly linear and there's nothing to them, it's basically like pac-man after seeing you once - they always know where you are. If you're expecting lethal company levels of uniqueness / polish to each enemy, turn away. All enemies in this boil down to similar things (except one is blind!). there's no interesting enemies here. They all have the exact same ai. They will chase you, know your exact path and then down you. And when you duck under a table and hide they will stare exactly where you are and then leave. The ai is terrible. They will sometimes even clip into the desk, get stuck, and make it so if you leave - you die. Which, compared to it's inspiration, (Lethal Company) Bracken's whole stalker mechanic, adds a whole set of fun fear. Yippee bug hoards items and sets up a region you want to avoid / risk. Dogs are blind and make you play around it / have interactions with other things (bait them to your jukebox, or buy items to bait them away from ship). Spiders set up and you have an area that you have to play around. Every enemy in that has a unique idea. None of that is in this game, it's playstation 1 ai thoroughly. Repeat about every single enemy. LC gives a toolbox of creatures that lead to awesome situations. None of that is here. Being chased you have one option to dodge an enemy, get under a table. otherwise even after you break line of sight and turn 4 different corners it will find you exacly where you are. Unless you're under a table, then it'll stand right infront of you, stare into your soul and leave. (NOT fixed) Get hit go down , except you do nothing for 12+mins other than crawl if your search buddy goes down too, and then the train leaves. (NOT fixed) And some of the comments by Vy, on their discord with someone who had similar issues to mine, they don't get the expectations of that person regarding unique monster design and it doesn't sound like anything cool is coming either. (NOT fixed) Animations / Enemy visuals. The enemies are the clunkiest goofiest looking things you’ll ever see. The spidey boys movements are clunky with a bizarrely awkward permanent facial expression. It walks like a stick rocking horse. (NOT fixed) Chainsaw guy has the awkward carry animation where he can walk for 10+mins with you in his hand and you’re exposed to his 3polygons for an hour. Being hit is like walking into an invisible hurt box with no visual feedback for anything. There’s no “dodging” swings, when an enemy is close, you get hurt. You only really tell you got hit because of the audio or instantly falling onto the floor. It feels cheap. Bugs : There's a ton of game breaking bugs at the moment or overall run ending bugs. Desync issues where people aren't seeing the same map. Doors being closed or openned for others. People being left behind by elevators. Items being different for others. Overall the co-op experience isn't very smooth. But they'll fix em for sure. (NOT fixed) Sound. (NOT fixed) Games like Lockdown Protocol have spacial audio sorted, this game doesn't even have it turned on. (made by a developer of the same size!) The store page states it muffles audio through walls / echoes. it doesn't. enemies 3 floors above you sound like they are in the room right beside and in front of you. this is maybe the hardest disappointment of it all for me personally. hopefully this gets changed. I bought it thinking I was getting into a game that was purposefully designed around audio / voice, and it’s really not true. At most, there's a reverb - and sound gets quieter further away. Dissapointing. Some jarring issues like enemies don't have any sort of footstep noise with some of the worst animations that go along with it (check out the lanky boy in the trailer, the spider) takes away from the horror a lot. Some things are REALLY well done, such as the alarms / metal detectors at least. Gameplay problems. --- It's stiff. It's janky. Some issue's I've had is that in a 12person lobby, It's impossible to tell people apart. There's no proper customisation for this, so everyone is near identical Name tags are tiny and illegible in movement (clips into the chest crouched too) No indicator mic is working when alive (many people I helped fixed on the first day had no idea we couldn't hear them) No indication you need to hold V either. Mobs walk through walls. Enemies can sometimes all freeze permanently. You can see through things by leaning. Enemies seemingly freeze up running on the spot 24/7 There isn't really much "co-op" in this. If someone messes up they go down(sometimes a cocoon or hook), you hold E to bring them back and that's it. There's no saving people from things are imminently gonna kill em. No sharing items between you all so people can cover seperate roles, or camera guy to help from afar. You can't deposit scrap til the train leaves. This leads to situations where you / players are too valuable to actually play more. So they afk in the train. Because calling the train ends the. Price point - not worth double letha

My friend and I picked up this game during the sale, but after playing it we’ve decided we’ll be requesting a refund. - Several times we died without clear cause. For example, while running from the chainsaw enemy we managed to get away, but then suddenly collapsed and were teleported back to the train. On the next run a message instructed us to “stop the bleeding,” yet there was no indication we were bleeding and we hadn’t been hit or seen an enemy. Deaths like these need clear, visible feedback so players understand what happened. - We bought equipment, but the train stopped and enemies appeared at the door and killed us instantly. After that, our purchased gear was gone. Thanks for that waste of money. - I play games for fun, and this one didn’t deliver. Looting feels unrewarding because item values aren’t visible at a glance, so you end up grabbing everything as a chore rather than enjoying the thrill of finding something valuable. Compare that to REPO, where finding a high-value item creates real excitement for the group. - The procedural levels feel bland and repetitive. It might be generated differently, but it sure does not feel like it. - The promised “unique” character progression is misleading. Customization is limited to cosmetic choices like color, sex, and age, which have no gameplay impact. Overall, this has been our least enjoyable experience in these kinds of games, and we won’t be revisiting it.

This is almost a recommended, and a few patches back I would have highly recommended this game based on how it was progressing and the direction it was headed. But the game took a massive detour with the Plantation update and has been losing sight of its original potential ever since. The game is basically Lethal Company but refocused as a horror game where you have to run and hide under tables. The atmosphere is creepy and the sound design is great, with eerie undertones and atmospheric sounds that give you a sense of fear and unease. In the early months of the game's release, it was fantastic. You were put in abandoned labyrinthine hotels and metros, with few but very clearly defined enemies that all had great tell on their location when near and very concise strategies to deal with them (Mostly running and hiding but in some cases juking). There were a few deadly entities prowling a huge level, so you had to weigh in the risks of proceeding further for loot and hoping for an elevator or turning back now. Then for some reason, the devs decide to change things up a notch. They added zombie hordes en masse, which are so plentiful that you will often get bitten quick which ends your run and forces a retreat. They added a human enemy that sprints at you with a gun to shoot you dead. This enemy just sucks to deal with, and completely hampers the intense but hopeful chase sequences the traditional entities offered. They added a map filled with a lot of traps, which sounds cool in theory but paired with the shotgunner is just plain awful as an experience. The devs originally added a Pentagon map that was a one and last chance to get a surge of loot to keep a doomed run going, then reneged on the core design and made the Pentagon extremely hard and filled with monsters because they didn't like the idea of players doing successful Pentagon runs. The hotel maps in earlier iterations had interesting backrooms-esque liminal large atrium rooms with multiple levels and rooms where you could use as a central hub and flower out your looting while keeping spatial memory, but the devs removed those rooms because it apparently didn't fit in with their concept of every room being a small, tight cell. Recently instead of designing new and interesting entities the devs took existing ones and super-fied them with insane speed and whatever. So now the entities which were originally fun and had ways to deal with are just a big "F you now F off" situation. Also small thing but the patch notes are extremely wordy lore pieces that obfuscate the actual gameplay stuff between lore text that Id much rather learn in game digetically. At the end of the day, its not a bad game per se. I just think that the devs are losing sight of what made the game fun in the first place, perhaps balancing in difficulty in unnecessary ways because a select few are doing too well. Making super speed monsters that excel at everything just to spike up the death rate doesn't make the game better, it just makes it tedious. The original cast had their flaws and strengths which made for interesting moments.

if you had asked me a few months ago if i would recommend this game, i would say absolutely... on the premise that the game was going to be updated and finished. as it stands now, i cant recommend this game anymore. the game still feels entirely unfinished and one dimensional. recent updates have changed the entire vibe and aesthetic of the game, taking it in a direction that seems to go astray from it's extraction horror roots. enemy ai often feels unfair and more like a nuisance to meta-game than an actual threat. in a world where you were once alone, just you and your teammates exploring barren maps searching for scraps, you now have... an npc on the train and (imo) out-of-theme enemies. maps feel like hallway simulators more than they do a labyrinth of rooms. and unfortunately, these issues will likely never be addressed, as the dev has stated that this game will no longer receive updates outside of maybe a bug fix here and there. with that considered, it unfortunately feels like a rushed and incomplete entry to the trending genre as a cash grab. sucks too, there was a basis for some good lore that never felt like it got fleshed out. if the game ever goes on sale for $10 or less, maybe worth a snag, but dont expect more than a few hours out of it.

[h1] [b] TL;DR [/b] If you want a scary horror game to play with your friends, Forsaken Frontiers is a good Lethal Company-like to pick up[/h1] [h3] Lethal Company Similarities and General Gameplay Loop [/h3] The first thing to get out of the way are the Lethal Company similarities, and I think this game is honestly a little easier than Lethal. The art style is similarly retro, but the gameplay loop is quite similar as well. In Forsaken Frontiers you start off in a train, run around a location collecting loot to sell while avoiding monsters, then return to said train to pay off your ever expanding debt until you can't anymore. There are a few notable differences though. Unlike Lethal Company, all of the maps (i.e. the Metro, the Hotel, the Hospital, the Bunker, the Plantation, etc.) have varied interiors, layouts and environmental hazards. Like Lethal Company, these maps can have map conditions that can either benefit, or hinder your ability to get loot. Beneficial ones are things like Vigor (which increases player stamina), Shadowstep (reduces noise player footsteps make) and Surplus (much more loot spawns in the map). Detrimental ones are things like Blackout (all lights in the map are out), Minefield (lots of mines spawn in the map), and Spores (you need a gas mask to enter the map and a new enemy type spawns). Note that not all of these maps are made equal, I personally hate the Hotel. Additionally, the loot you collect in these maps does not take up inventory space, meaning you can just run around picking up however much you want until you need to run back to the train before it departs without you. The downside to this though is that the loot you find doesn't have utility functions since their sole purpose is to be sold. This means that you won't find loot like the stop signs in Lethal Company or the clown bomb in REPO. [h3] The Entities [/h3] Most of the entities in this game are for the most part more fair than you would initially think, since they each have at least one main counter. Normally, I wouldn't really want to spoil the entities too much but I think it's worth talking about them since I know they can be frustrating if you don't know their mechanics. The Spider, which looks like a large, lanky dude that walks on all fours, is blind, so as long as you aren't making that much noise you should be fine. Previously the Spider had a "sensing" ability that could bypass this blindness but the latest update removed this ability, so it's much more fair than it was before. The Forsaken, which are infected people who scream a lot will try to bite you to infect you (and the infection will kill you after a set amount of time) but will leave you alone once you're infected, meaning they can't kill you directly if you have enough time to escape. There is one enemy that feels rather unfair though, and that is the Butcher, who is a big dude with a chainsaw. For some reason this guy just does not lose aggro easily, and sometimes when you feel like you should have lost him he'll still be chasing you. Another problem with this guy is that he always spawns in the very first map players will experience, so his mechanics can make it frustrating for new players. Also even though the game doesn't really say so, YOU CAN HIDE FROM MONSTERS. There will be desks scattered around in the maps that have a little space underneath to hide in, and there is no limit to how many players can hide in them. Although, if an entity sees you enter the desk there is a high chance they'll kill you anyways so be sure to break line of sight before you hide. It's worth it to mention that the recent update added dynamite you can buy from the shop that you can use to straight up kill any entity so if there's a specific enemy you really hate you can just...kill them now. [h3] The Items [/h3] As you would expect, this game has a shop that you can use to buy items to help you survive in your treks into the various maps. Some of these items are nice little quality of life tools, while others are straight up game changers. The Stun Light, Sledgehammer and Dynamite all allow you powerful options for dealing with the entities in this game. So if you're struggling, try those ones out. [h3] Bugs [/h3] For the most part I haven't encountered that many bugs in this game though they do exist and even though they didn't bother me that much I thought I should mention them. The Bunker map always seems to have at least one hole in the floor of the map that players (other than the host) can fall through to teleport themselves back to the train. Honestly, I thought this bug was pretty funny when I first saw it. Also on the Bunker map, there was one time where I was downed after an entity saw me hide under a desk but my character glitched out of the map and was thus teleported back to the train and thus to safety. I guess the takeaway here is that the Bunker map is just a little janky. The Spider used to have what felt like a bug of the sensing ability where he could randomly know where you were even if you were completely silent, but this bug should be gone after the sensing ability was flat out removed. Sometimes when a player joins the host before a round starts, they'll be disconnected if they buy anything from the shop. This can be worked around by just having the host buy the items and having the affected player pick up the items from the shop counter or from the ground. There was also this one bug where our leftover money carried over to a subsequent run after we couldn't pay our debt. Overall if you are someone who likes co-op horror games or just wants to play a Lethal Company-like horror game then I would recommend Forsaken Frontiers.

[h2] My Favorite Lethal Company by Far [/h2] Forsaken Frontiers has soul and, what initially caught my attention, it's a genuine horror game with good ambiance. After 25 hours of playing it, my friends and I have still not gone through all of its content, due to recurring updates from the devs. I have also yet to be able to master avoiding quite a few of its monsters, which means it's not a shallow game that gets you bored quickly or that's easy, with no variation between enemies themselves. [b] It's got issues: [/b] It's has a handful of run-ruining bugs, like the Shepherd always finding you under a table (sometimes), players other than the host seeing through walls and being able to teleport back to the train, players being invisible. I wanted to like this game but was disappointed. Visuals looked good and accomplished what I assume the dev was going for, sounds were good if not a bit loud at some points, especially on the train, gameplay loop left a lot to be desired. Loot capacity is unlimited and doesn't give much reason for players to return to the train, allowing them to get more or and more lost. While this may have been the intention, it leads to rummaging around until you are lucky enough to run into the elevator or for the enemies to spawn, and then wait for the inevitable lock on and never ending chase. The monsters unfortunately, are the low point of this game. Of the ones I ran into consistently, the butcher is completely broken in his ability to heat seek onto a player until they run out of stamina (special shoutout to the entity that puts you in the backrooms, which is interesting the first time and annoying the next 6 times).
